clue.text: Superficial American backing France in competition

indicators.note: backing means the word for American is read backwards, from the back
in signals France goes inside the competition word

parts.note: a race is a competition
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: A shallow American, sponsoring a French entry in some contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like financial support, but it is the turnaround signal acting on the American.
explanation.definitionFit: Superficial describes something on the outside only; as a noun the answer means the outer face, and it is used attributively for skin-deep things.

clue.text: Devilish women mostly besetting male? Give in

indicators.note: besetting means the shortened word surrounds the male letter
mostly means the last letter of the demons word is dropped

parts.note: succubi are female demons

explanation.surface: Female demons nearly surrounding a man: will he yield?
explanation.walkthrough: SUCCUB, mostly SUCCUBI, wraps M between its second U and B.
explanation.definitionFit: To succumb is to yield or surrender to pressure or temptation, which is to give in.

clue.text: Get to dispute losing book

indicators.note: losing means the book letter is taken away

parts.note: a breach is a rift or quarrel

explanation.surface: To get round to arguing without the book to hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a place is to arrive at it, so the verb is a synonym of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: M and S are perhaps primarily represented with this?

definitions.text: M and S are perhaps primarily represented with this?

indicators.note: represented means the letters are rendered in a new form, rearranged
primarily means the first letter of the word perhaps

explanation.surface: A chain store's name, Marks and Spencer, written in its short form with a symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: M&S is written with the & sign, which is what the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampersand is the & sign that stands for and, as in the abbreviation M&S.

clue.text: Bet swapping bridge partner will make you keen

indicators.note: swapping means one letter of the bet word is exchanged for another

parts.note: a wager is a bet
in bridge West partners East, so W is swapped for its partner E

explanation.surface: A wager with a change of card partner is something you'll be keen on.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge seats are North, South, East and West; West and East play as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means keenly wanting to do something, so it is a synonym for keen.

clue.text: Singular revolutionary group almost capturing mountain in component of operation

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: capturing means the shortened group word holds the mountain inside it
almost means the last letter of the group word is dropped

parts.note: a cell is a small group of revolutionaries working in secret
an alp is a mountain

explanation.surface: A lone band of revolutionaries seizing a peak as part of a military operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operation' sounds military, but it is surgical: the answer is a tool used in an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's knife is an essential instrument in any surgical procedure, so it is a component of an operation.

clue.text: Think a lot of ditching soldiers and airman, hosting large display

indicators.note: ditching means the soldiers' letters are discarded

parts.note: to respect someone is to think a lot of them
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of soldiers

indicators.note: hosting means the airman word holds the large letter inside

parts.note: an ace is a skilled fighter pilot
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Admiring a display of flying after the troops leave and a pilot puts on a big show.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is an impressive visual show or performance, so it is a display.

clue.text: Justice principally absent from the way some people talk or gas

indicators.note: absent from means that letter is removed from the talk word

parts.note: jargon is the specialist speech of a group

indicators.note: principally means the first letter of the word justice

explanation.surface: Without justice, some folk's speech is just hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' could mean idle talk, fitting the surface, but it is the chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is a noble gas, the third most abundant in the air, so it is an example of a gas.

clue.text: 3 or 5? It's 4 coming within that — very basic

indicators.note: coming within means the other pieces go inside the prime word

parts.note: 3 and 5 are examples of prime numbers
it, with 's as is linking to the number
IV is 4 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A number puzzle: is 3 or 5 prime, and is 4 inside it? How elementary.
explanation.walkthrough: The digits are not cross-references: 3 and 5 are primes and 4 is IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Primitive means crude and rudimentary, at an early stage of development, which is very basic.

clue.text: Hidden state is behind source of confusion in US state

parts.note: to be late is to be behind time

indicators.note: in means that letter goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York

indicators.note: source of means the first letter of the word confusion

explanation.surface: A secret state lags behind a confused state in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden state' looks political, but it is the definition: latency is a dormant condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Latency is the condition of being present but not yet visible or active, a concealed condition.

clue.text: Time for winner to receive new wine?

parts.note: a champ (champion) is a winner

indicators.note: to receive means the time word takes the new letter inside it

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: It's time to give the victor some freshly made wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the answer is one example of wine, the one winners spray about.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparkling white from a French region is a wine, so the answer is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Instinctive to accept one criminal's ultimate responsibility

indicators.note: to accept means the instinctive word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a gut reaction is an instinctive one
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: ultimate means the last letter of the word criminal

parts.note: the word criminal, whose last letter is used; the 's links to what follows

explanation.surface: A gut feeling that one criminal ultimately bears the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of criminal's is possessive, attaching the final letter to criminal; the picked letter is L, not S.
explanation.definitionFit: Guilt is the fact of being to blame for a wrongdoing, which is culpability, a kind of responsibility.

clue.text: Drug dealer ignoring first court official

indicators.note: ignoring first means the dealer word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a pusher sells drugs

explanation.surface: A dealer who doesn't put himself first ends up as a court functionary.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher keeps order and shows people to their places in a law court, a recognised courtroom role.

clue.text: Holding teacher's latest school punishment, allowing daughter out

indicators.note: latest means the final letter of the word teacher

parts.note: the word teacher, whose last letter is used

indicators.note: with allowing, out means the daughter letter is let go from the punishment word

parts.note: detention is being kept in after school as a punishment
D is the genealogy abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A teacher's latest after-school detention, though the daughter is allowed to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Allowing ... out' is the removal signal, split around the daughter it lets go.
explanation.definitionFit: Retention is the act of keeping or holding on to something, so the noun 'holding' is a synonym.

clue.text: Grandiose failure receiving a significant portion of blame

indicators.note: receiving means the failure and blame pieces together take the a inside them

parts.note: a bomb is a flop, a failure

indicators.note: most of the blame word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to get stick is to get blamed or criticised

explanation.surface: A spectacular flop that attracts a big share of the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: Stick is British slang for criticism or blame, as in 'take stick'; the a sits where the failure meets the shortened blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombastic speech is inflated and pompous, the overblown style also called grandiose.

clue.text: French designer not finishing dressing the converted religious follower

indicators.note: dressing means the shortened designer word is wrapped around the other letters
not finishing means the designer word loses its last letter

parts.note: a modiste is a fashion designer or milliner, a French word

indicators.note: converted means the letters of the are changed round

explanation.surface: A French couturier, mid-job, clothing someone who has converted to a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Modiste is a French word for a dressmaker or milliner, used in English too.
explanation.definitionFit: A Methodist belongs to the Protestant church founded by John Wesley, so is a follower of a religion.

clue.text: A small guy's tucked into drink (a large quantity of the drink)

definitions.text: a large quantity of the drink

indicators.note: tucked into means the pieces go inside the drink word

parts.note: tea is a drink
a man is a guy; with 's it gives MANS

explanation.surface: A short chap downs a drink, though the bracket says it's a vast amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the sea, so the bracket is the definition: a sea is a lot of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tasman Sea lies between Australia and New Zealand; 'the drink' is slang for the sea, of which it is a part.

clue.text: Big shot taking last of paper in back yard toilet

indicators.note: back means the big shot with its added letter is read in reverse
taking means the big shot word takes the paper's final letter inside

parts.note: a VIP is a very important person, a big shot

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of the word paper

explanation.surface: A bigwig grabbing the last of the paper in an outdoor loo out the back.
explanation.walkthrough: VIP reversed is PIV, and R goes in after its P.
explanation.definitionFit: A privy is an old word for a lavatory, especially an outdoor one, so it is a synonym for toilet.

clue.text: Long day in estate — how might the night look?

indicators.note: in means the other pieces go inside the estate word

parts.note: a park is the grounds of a country estate
to itch is to long for something

explanation.surface: A long day on a country estate, and how dark the night might seem.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch-dark means completely black, the description of a moonless night.

clue.text: Fine time to promote energy, making a stink

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: to promote means the energy letter moves up to the front of the time word

parts.note: tide is an old word for time, as in Christmastide
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A nice moment to push energy policy, causing a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: TIDE with its E brought to the top becomes ETID.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fetid smells foul, so it is giving off a stench; the adjective matches the participle phrase.

clue.text: Particular person reduced safeguard, leading to awkward situation

indicators.note: reduced means the safeguard word loses its last letter

parts.note: a fuse is an electrical safety device
to be in a spot is to be in a tricky situation

explanation.surface: Cutting back on safety precautions lands someone in a tight corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Particular' means fussy here, not specific.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusspot is someone overly fastidious, and particular means fussy, so it names such a person.

clue.text: Meet distractedly during hard work for a sugar boost?

indicators.note: during means the jumbled letters sit inside the hard-work word

parts.note: sweat is hard toil

indicators.note: distractedly suggests the letters of meet are jumbled

explanation.surface: Meeting someone absent-mindedly while toiling, and needing a sugar rush.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a playful definition: a sweet treat as an energy hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetmeat is a candied confection, so eating one gives a hit of sugar.

clue.text: Pledged to a place (not America)

indicators.note: not means the America letter is left out

parts.note: stead means place, as in in his stead

explanation.surface: A toast pledged to a place outside the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast someone is to raise a glass in their honour, a drinking pledge; the past tense matches.

clue.text: Lack indication of early New England winter?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a deficit, an amount by which something falls short

definitions.text: indication of early New England winter?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: a brief autumn (Americans say fall) means winter comes early

explanation.walkthrough: Fall is the American word for autumn; a short one would bring winter early to New England.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortfall is a deficit, the amount by which supply fails to meet need, so it is a lack.

clue.text: Symbolic English author Left dismissed I also abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means the I is also dropped from what remains
dismissed means the left letter is sent away

parts.note: J R R Tolkien was an English author

explanation.surface: An English writer of symbolism, with the Left and the narrator both cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, token means done for show, a nominal gesture, so it is symbolic.

clue.text: Pub that won't put you all out

definitions.meaning: first meaning: your ... is your nearby pub

definitions.text: that won't put you all out
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a ... anaesthetic numbs only part of you, unlike a general one that knocks you out

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is the pub near your home. 'Put out' also means knock unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: A local anaesthetic numbs one area while the patient stays awake; and a neighbourhood pub is a local.

clue.text: Mediterranean port provided answer after show of surprise

indicators.note: after means the provided and answer pieces follow the surprise piece

parts.note: ha! is an exclamation of surprise
if means provided, as in provided that

explanation.surface: A port is named once someone has reacted with surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Haifa is a major seaport city in northern Israel on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Italy discouraging adopting old form of expression

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: adopting means the discouraging word takes the old letter inside

parts.note: dim prospects are discouraging ones

explanation.surface: Italy, depressingly, taking on an outdated turn of phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed phrase whose sense is not literal, so it is a particular way of saying something.

clue.text: Sharp point right in something probing locks

indicators.note: in means the right letter goes inside the pick word

parts.note: a pick (lockpick) is the tool used to probe a lock

explanation.surface: A spiky tip held in a burglar's tool for fiddling with locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' could be hair, but here a pick probes door locks.
explanation.definitionFit: A prick is a small sharp point, such as a thorn, or the mark one makes.

clue.text: Conservative, one at the top level, but initially very left-wing

indicators.note: initially means the very piece is put first, before the others

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
I is the Roman numeral for one
A-list describes the top level of celebrities

explanation.surface: A Tory at the highest rank turns out, at first, to be a radical leftie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very left-wing' looks like the definition, but 'very' belongs to the wordplay and 'initially' says where its piece goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Socialism sits on the political left, so the adjective for it means left-wing.

clue.text: Liner incomplete, needing a queen's name

indicators.note: incomplete means the liner's name loses its last letter

parts.note: the Titanic was a famous ocean liner

explanation.surface: A cut-down ocean liner needs a regal name.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania is the fairy queen in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, so it is a queen's name.

clue.text: Stop short by lady, backtracking intently

indicators.note: backtracking means the whole combination is read backwards

parts.note: a dame is a lady

indicators.note: short means the stop word loses its last letter

parts.note: to kill an engine is to stop it

explanation.surface: Pulling up beside a woman, then retracing one's steps with great concentration.
explanation.walkthrough: KIL plus DAME gives KILDAME, which read backwards spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with great energy or intensity, wholeheartedly, is the idiom's sense; intently fits.
